hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are basking in vindication over Manchester City's 115 charges finally catching up to them, with a strong 'we told you so' energy directed at City's players and their past snide remarks. There's righteous anger at how City's financial doping poached talent from rivals and distorted the league, mixed with cautious optimism about Arsenal's own trajectory — Gyokeres and Merino transfer talk included. The mood is less 'we've won the league' and more 'justice is finally being served, and our time is coming.'

daily.summary: The day began with measured transfer speculation and cautious optimism (6/10), deteriorated into frustration over attacking deficiencies and squad concerns by midday (4/10), and erupted into incandescent fury by nightfall (2/10) following Manchester City's £900m financial fraud revelations. The dominant trajectory is a sharp, accelerating decline into existential rage, with the City scandal retroactively poisoning memories of past title near-misses and overriding all other narratives.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment swung wildly across the week, defined by extreme daily volatility rather than a steady trend. A mid-week peak of vindicated schadenfreude over Manchester City's 115-charge verdict (7/10) provided the emotional high, but this quickly curdled into cynicism as focus returned to Arsenal's own injury crisis, transfer frustrations, and a stunning end to the Women's team's 20-game unbeaten run. Contract security for Arteta and Rice bookended the period as rare stabilizers, but the dominant experience was whiplash — euphoria, panic, and frustration often within the same 24 hours.
